last.verdict: Opendoor is buying homes far faster than it sells them, and profit per home and losses are both heading the wrong way.

takeaways.label: Profit per home shrinking
takeaways.text: Contribution margin fell to 3.3% from 5.8% last quarter, with profit per home sold at $12K versus $22K. The company expects contribution profit dollars to decline again in Q4.

takeaways.label: Bigger losses guided
takeaways.text: Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss is guided to $70M-$85M, versus $31M in Q3 and $4M in Q2. The Q3 net loss was $218M.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt ballooning
takeaways.text: Opendoor bought 4,865 homes but sold 2,728, lifting inventory to $2.57B. About $2.0B of bank loans against those homes now falls due within a year; cash is $910M.

takeaways.label: Growth continues
takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $1.02B, up 12% from a year ago. Q4 revenue is guided to grow at least 40% year over year, against $736M last year.

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
